newsitem.title: USA: Firearms Training sees FY 97 EPS $0.60.
newsitem.headline: Firearms Training sees FY 97 EPS $0.60.

text.p: The chief financial officer of Firearms Training Systems Inc said he supports Wall Street's consensus earnings of $0.60 a share for the 1997 fiscal year that ended March 31.
"Yes, we're comfortable with it," CFO David Apseloff told Reuters Monday night after he spoke to analysts at the annual institutional conference of the Robinson-Humphrey Co Inc.
He said Firearms Training, which went public in November, will announce earnings in mid-May.
Apseloff expressed no disagreement with Wall Street consensus earnings forecast of $0.75 a share for fiscal 1998.
"They have a reasonable basis for that estimate," Apseloff said.

During the company's presentation to analysts, its president, Peter Marino, said the firm is trying to expand into new markets. The company makes and sells video simulations on firearms training primarily to the military and police departments.

Budget-cutting by the U.S. military because of the end of the Cold War is helping rather than hurting growth, Marino said. The U.S. Army and Marine Corps, he said, are finding that using video to simulate combat conditions saves money because relatively little live ammunition is spent during training.

Marino said the company has targeted several new markets including the hunter safety field. Many states require people to undergo firearms training when they receive hunting licenses. Another potential mrkets is the security guard industry, Marino said.
